- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above recent high.
- If sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., +1 then -1), model overreacts to short-term sentiment; smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values.
- Model underestimates true volatility in high-sentiment periods (especially +1 sentiment); increase forecast by 1–3% for sentiment >0.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model holds too high; adjust downward by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–2 days; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative entries, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to counteract bias.
- In high-sentiment +1 periods, model often fails to capture upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for each +1 sentiment day.
